newsitem.title: ERITREA: Sudan rebels claim victory in renewed fighting.
newsitem.headline: Sudan rebels claim victory in renewed fighting.

text.p: Rebels of the Sudan People's Liberation Army (SPLA) have captured the town of Kaya near the Uganda border and are advancing on the main south Sudan town of Juba, an SPLA spokesman said in Asmara on Sunday.

Yassir Arman told Reuters: "The SPLA forces launched a simultaneous attack on Kaya and the Yei-Juba road and captured Kaya town. Our forces are three kilometres (two miles) from Yei town. We will capture it at any time."
The rebel claim was the first indication for several weeks of the progress of their offensive launched in January, when areas bordering Eritrea were captured.
Kaya, west of the Nile, is only 30 km (20 miles) north of the Uganda border, and 70 km (44 miles) east of Yei, a key centre close to the Zaire border.

Arman said the rebel forces had also attacked Morobo, and had captured Gumuni garrison on the Yei-Juba road. The headquarters of the National Tobacco Company near Gumuni was also in SPLA hands, he said.
Arman said fighting took place around Juba on Sunday but that no details were available.

The SPLA, led by John Garang, has been fighting the Khartoum government since 1983, demanding independence for the mainly Christian and animist south of the Sudan against the Moslem and Arabised north.
Khartoum accuses Uganda of supporting the SPLA -- a charge denied by Uganda.
